definition_zh: 责任；义务；职责；税；值班
definition_en: a moral or legal obligation, a task that belongs to a job, a tax on goods, or a period of work
core_image: 肩上压着一块木牌，上面写着「必须做」
scene: 夜班护士在交班时把记录本递过去，走廊的灯仍亮着。The nurse finished her duty at dawn and handed over the notes.
sceneCN: 这里 duty 是「值班」（第 4 个义项：一段时间内的工作班次）；句意是那名护士天亮时值完班，把记录本交了出去。

pos.zh: 名词：责任；义务；职责；税；值班

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「尽职的；孝顺的」
由 dutiful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「尽职地；恭顺地」
由本词与 free 复合，义为「免税的」

senses.title: A moral or legal obligation
senses.definition: something that a person must do because it is morally right or required by law
senses.definitionCN: 因为道德上正确或法律要求而必须做的事
senses.example: He felt a duty to tell the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得自己有责任说出真相。
senses.why: Duty began as what is owed, and an obligation is a debt that is not counted in money.
senses.whyCN: duty 最初指「所欠之物」，而义务就是一笔不用钱来计数的债。

senses.title: A task belonging to a job
senses.definition: a responsibility or task that comes with a particular position or role
senses.definitionCN: 伴随某个职位或角色而来的责任或任务
senses.example: The guard's duties include checking every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 保安的职责包括检查每一位来访者。
senses.why: A job assigns specific things that must be done, so the abstract debt becomes a concrete list of tasks.
senses.whyCN: 一份工作会指派必须完成的具体事项，于是抽象的「欠」变成一张具体的任务清单。

senses.title: A tax on goods
senses.definition: a tax paid on goods, especially goods brought into a country
senses.definitionCN: 对货物所征的税，尤指进口货物
senses.example: The government raised the duty on cigarettes.
senses.exampleCN: 政府提高了香烟的税。
senses.why: A payment owed to the state for goods follows the same debt image, so duty also names a customs charge.
senses.whyCN: 因货物而欠国家的款项沿用同一个债务意象，所以 duty 也指海关征收的税。

senses.title: A period of work
senses.definition: a period during which someone is working, especially in a hospital, the army or a hotel
senses.definitionCN: 某人正在工作的一段时间，尤指医院、军队或酒店中的班次
senses.example: The nurse finished her duty at dawn and handed over the notes.
senses.exampleCN: 那名护士天亮时值完班，把记录本交了出去。
senses.why: The time when one is on duty is the time one owes to the job, so the obligation is measured out in shifts.
senses.whyCN: 一个人 on duty 的时间就是欠给工作的时间，于是义务被按班次量了出来。

intro.en: Duty comes from Old French deu, the past participle of devoir, to owe, and devoir goes back to Latin debere.
intro.cn: duty 来自古法语 deu，即 devoir（欠）的过去分词，而 devoir 又可追溯到拉丁语 debere。

items.en: Latin debere meant to owe or to be under an obligation, and it also produced debt and debit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 debere 意为「欠」或「负有义务」，还生出 debt 与 debit。

items.en: The past participle debitum meant something owed, and from it came the noun for a debt.
items.cn: 过去分词 debitum 意为「所欠之物」，由此产生表示债务的名词。

items.en: The verb devoir meant to owe or to be obliged, and its participle deu meant owed or fitting.
items.cn: 动词 devoir 意为「欠、应当」，其分词 deu 意为「所欠的、应有的」。

items.en: The noun deute named what is owed, including both moral obligations and payments.
items.cn: 名词 deute 指所欠之物，既包括道德义务，也包括应付款项。

items.en: Middle English dute carried the senses of obligation, service and a customary payment.
items.cn: 中古英语 dute 兼具「义务、服务、惯常应缴款项」几层意思。

items.en: The tax sense and the shift sense settled alongside the moral sense, giving the word its present range.
items.cn: 税与班次两个义项与道德义并存固定下来，形成今天这个词的义域。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on duty; the near-meaning group separates obligation, responsibility, task and tax by what is owed.
note.cn: 形近组收由 duty 构成的词形；近义组按所欠之物区分 obligation、responsibility、task 与 tax。

entries.definition: Doing what duty requires; formed from duty with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「尽职的、孝顺的」，由 duty 加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: In a manner that fulfils duty; dutiful plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「尽职地、恭顺地」，由 dutiful 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Exempt from the tax called duty; duty plus free.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「免税的」，由 duty 加 free 构成。

entries.definition: Owed or expected; both due and duty descend from the same French participle.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「应付的、预定的」，与 duty 同出同一个法语分词。

entries.definition: A moral or legal requirement; more formal and more binding than duty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「义务、责任」，比 duty 更正式、约束力更强。

entries.definition: The state of being in charge of something and answerable for it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「责任、负责」，指对某事负有掌管与交代之责。

entries.definition: A piece of work to be done; concrete, and without the moral weight of duty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「任务」，具体而不带 duty 的道德分量。

entries.definition: A tax on imports or exports; a technical trade word for the tax sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「关税」，是 duty 税义在贸易领域的专业说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the French participle for owed and then spread it across moral duty, job tasks, taxes and shifts.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从法语中表示「所欠」的分词出发，再把它铺到道德责任、工作职责、税与班次上。

normal.en: Duty and due share one origin: what is owed.
normal.cn: duty 与 due 同源，核心都是「所欠之物」。

normal.en: A moral duty is a debt no one can pay for you.
normal.cn: 道德上的 duty 是一笔别人替你还不了的债。

normal.en: A job turns duty into a list: duties are the tasks written into the role.
normal.cn: 工作把 duty 变成一张清单：duties 就是写进职位里的任务。

normal.en: A customs duty is money owed to the state for goods.
normal.cn: customs duty 就是因为货物而欠国家的钱。

normal.en: On duty and off duty measure the debt in hours.
normal.cn: on duty 与 off duty 用小时来计量这笔债。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden sign tied to a pair of shoulders, reading: must be done.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木牌绑在一副肩膀上，上面写着：必须做。

abstract.en: The same sign can be a law, a job description, a customs form or a hospital rota.
abstract.cn: 同一块牌子可以是一条法律、一份职位说明、一张海关单或一张医院排班表。

abstract.en: Duty is everything owed, whether to conscience, to an employer, to a state or to a ward.
abstract.cn: duty 是所有欠下的东西，无论欠的是良心、雇主、国家还是一个病房。

examples.en: He felt a duty to tell the truth.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己有责任说出真相。

examples.en: The guard's duties include checking every visitor.
examples.cn: 保安的职责包括检查每一位来访者。

examples.en: The nurse finished her duty at dawn.
examples.cn: 那名护士天亮时值完班。

dict_mnemonic.text: due 是「应付的」，duty 就是应付的那一份：对良心是责任，对工作是职责，对货物是税。

root: 经由古法语 deu（devoir 的过去分词，意为「所欠的、应有的」）来自拉丁语 debere「欠、负有义务」，与 due、debt、debit 同源。中古英语 dute 起兼有责任、服务与应缴款项诸义，后来固定为今天的四个主要义项。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of duty all name something owed: to conscience, to a job, to the state, or to a shift.
sensesIntro.cn: duty 的四个义项都在命名某种「欠」：欠良心的、欠工作的、欠国家的，或欠一个班次的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden sign tied to a pair of shoulders, reading must be done.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木牌绑在肩膀上，写着「必须做」。

branches.en: THE CONSCIENCE: a debt that is moral or legal rather than financial.
branches.cn: 良心线：一笔道德或法律上的债，而非金钱之债。

branches.en: THE JOB: the abstract debt becomes a written list of tasks.
branches.cn: 工作线：抽象的债变成一张写好的任务清单。

branches.en: THE BORDER: money owed to the state for goods crossing it.
branches.cn: 边境线：货物过境时欠国家的钱。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the debt measured out in working hours and shifts.
branches.cn: 时钟线：用工作小时和班次来量这笔债。

branches.en: ONE BIND: conscience, job and shift are three ways of saying what one owes.
branches.cn: 同一种约束：良心、工作与班次，是「欠」的三种说法。

intro.en: Duty is a French-Latin noun; English adds -ful, -ly and the compound -free.
intro.cn: duty 是源自法语的拉丁系名词；英语加 -ful、-ly，并构成 -free 复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin debere and debitum are recorded, and the French branch devoir, deu and deute is also well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 debere 与 debitum 均有记录，法语一支的 devoir、deu、deute 也有充分书证。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基础。

items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是最深层的来源。

definition_zh: 染料；染色；染上颜色
definition_en: a substance used to give colour to cloth, hair or other materials, to colour something with it, or to give a deep lasting colour
core_image: 一块白布浸进深蓝色的染缸，提起来时颜色已经吃进纤维
scene: 作坊里一口大染缸冒着热气，白布被慢慢浸下去。The cloth was soaked in a blue dye.
sceneCN: 这里 dye 是「染料」（第 1 个义项：给织物上色的物质）；句意是那块布被浸在蓝色染料里。

pos.zh: 名词：染料；染液
动词：给……染色；使染上颜色

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「染工；染色者」
由本词与 stuff 复合，义为「染料；着色剂」
由 dyed 与 in the wool 组成的习语，义为「彻头彻尾的；顽固的」

senses.title: A colouring substance
senses.definition: a natural or chemical substance used to give colour to cloth, hair or other materials
senses.definitionCN: 用来给布料、头发或其他材料上色的天然或化学物质
senses.example: The cloth was soaked in a blue dye.
senses.exampleCN: 那块布被浸在蓝色染料里。
senses.why: This is the concrete core: a substance whose only job is to transfer colour into a material.
senses.whyCN: 这是具体的核心：一种唯一任务就是把颜色送进材料里的物质。

senses.title: To colour with a dye
senses.definition: to give something a colour by putting it into a dye or applying dye to it
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放进染液或把染料涂上去，使其带有颜色
senses.example: She dyed her coat dark green.
senses.exampleCN: 她把外套染成了深绿色。
senses.why: The verb is the noun in action: the substance enters the material and changes its colour.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词在动作中：物质进入材料，改变了它的颜色。

senses.title: To colour deeply or lastingly
senses.definition: to give something a strong or lasting colour, often used of light or of a figurative change
senses.definitionCN: 给某物强烈的或持久的颜色，常用于光线或比喻性的变化
senses.example: The sunset dyed the sky orange.
senses.exampleCN: 落日把天空染成了橙色。
senses.why: Once a dye is fixed, the colour will not wash out, so the verb extends to any deep and lasting tint.
senses.whyCN: 染料一旦固定，颜色就洗不掉，于是这个动词扩展到任何浓重而持久的着色。

intro.en: Dye is a native Old English word for colour and for the act of colouring, later narrowed to the substance and its use.
intro.cn: dye 是本族语古英语词，原指颜色与上色的动作，后来收窄为染料及其使用。

items.en: A Germanic noun and verb for colouring are reconstructed, though the exact forms and their deeper origin are uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中被重构出表示「上色」的名词与动词，但其确切形式与更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English had a noun for colour or dye and a verb meaning to colour, both from the same family.
items.cn: 古英语有表示「颜色、染料」的名词，也有表示「上色」的动词，二者同属一族。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun for the substance and the verb for the action, and the spelling moved toward dye.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了表示物质的名词和表示动作的动词，拼写逐渐走向 dye。

items.en: Dyeing became a major trade, and dye, dyer and dyestuff fixed the workshop vocabulary.
items.cn: 染色在十六世纪成为重要行业，dye、dyer、dyestuff 固定了作坊里的词汇。

items.en: The figurative sense of colouring light or a mood appears alongside the industrial sense.
items.cn: 给光线或情绪「染色」的比喻义与工业义同时存在。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dye and one dangerous near-spelling; the near-meaning group separates colouring verbs by strength and method.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dye 构成的词形和一个易混拼写；近义组按强度与方法区分几个着色动词。

entries.definition: A person whose trade is dyeing cloth; dye plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「染工」，由 dye 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Any substance used as a dye; dye plus stuff.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「染料、着色剂」，由 dye 加 stuff 构成。

entries.definition: The process of colouring cloth; spelled with e to distinguish it from dying.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「染色工艺」，保留 e 是为了与 dying 区分。

entries.definition: The present participle of die; it sounds the same as dyeing but has no colour in it.
entries.definitionCN: die 的现在分词，与 dyeing 同音，却与颜色无关。

entries.definition: To give colour to something; the general verb, usable for paint, dye or light.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给……上色」，通用词，可指颜料、染料或光。

entries.definition: To leave a mark or colour that is hard to remove, often accidentally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「弄脏、染上痕迹」，常指意外留下难去的颜色。

entries.definition: To give a slight colour to something; softer and lighter than dye.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给……淡淡上色」，比 dye 更轻更浅。

entries.definition: A dry colouring matter used in paint; a material rather than the action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「颜料」，是涂料中的干性着色物质，指材料而非动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the colour from the vat into the fibre and then into the sky at sunset.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着颜色从染缸进入纤维，再进入落日的天空。

normal.en: Dye is the substance; to dye is to put that substance into a material.
normal.cn: dye 是物质，to dye 是把这种物质送进材料。

normal.en: A dyer works with dye, and a dyestuff is any material that dyes.
normal.cn: dyer 与 dye 打交道，dyestuff 是任何能染色的材料。

normal.en: Dyeing keeps the e; dying from die does not, so the spelling marks the difference.
normal.cn: dyeing 保留 e，来自 die 的 dying 不留，拼写标出了区别。

normal.en: A blue dye in a vat can turn a whole bolt of cloth blue.
normal.cn: 染缸里的一缸蓝色染料能把整匹布染蓝。

normal.en: Sunset dyeing the sky is the same image, with light as the dye.
normal.cn: 落日染天空是同一个意象，只是光成了染料。

abstract.en: Picture white cloth disappearing into dark blue liquid and coming out changed.
abstract.cn: 想象白布没入深蓝的液体，再出来时已经变了颜色。

abstract.en: The same liquid, thinner, could be a tint; the same mark, accidental, could be a stain.
abstract.cn: 同样的液体淡一些就是 tint；同样的痕迹若是意外留下，就是 stain。

abstract.en: Dye is colour deciding to stay rather than sit on the surface.
abstract.cn: dye 是颜色决定留下来，而不是停在表面。

examples.en: The cloth was soaked in a blue dye.
examples.cn: 那块布被浸在蓝色染料里。

examples.en: She dyed her coat dark green.
examples.cn: 她把外套染成了深绿色。

examples.en: The sunset dyed the sky orange.
examples.cn: 落日把天空染成了橙色。

dict_mnemonic.text: dye 是一缸颜色：把布浸进去，颜色就吃进纤维，再也洗不掉。

root: 本族语古英语词，原有表示「颜色、染料」的名词与表示「上色」的动词，中古英语拼写逐渐固定为 dye。十六世纪染色业兴盛，dyer、dyestuff 等词进入作坊词汇。更早的日耳曼语形式与印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of dye move from the substance, to the act of applying it, to any deep and lasting colouring.
sensesIntro.cn: dye 的三个义项从染料这一物质，移到施加它的动作，再到任何浓重而持久的着色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white cloth sinking into a vat of dark blue liquid.
core.cn: 核心意象：白布沉入一缸深蓝的染液。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: the material whose purpose is to carry colour.
branches.cn: 物质线：以携带颜色为目的的材料。

branches.en: THE BATH: the cloth enters the liquid and comes out changed.
branches.cn: 染缸线：布进入液体，出来时已经变了颜色。

branches.en: THE LASTING TINT: colour that stays, even when the dye is light.
branches.cn: 持久着色线：颜色留了下来，即使染的是光。

branches.en: MATTER AND ACTION: the substance and the act share one name in English.
branches.cn: 物质与动作：物质和动作在英语里共用一个词。

branches.en: FROM CLOTH TO SKY: the same verb colours fabric and evening light.
branches.cn: 从布到天空：同一个动词既染织物，也染暮色。

intro.en: Dye is a native word; English builds dyer, dyestuff and dyeing with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: dye 是本族语词；英语用普通后缀构成 dyer、dyestuff 与 dyeing。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; Latin tingere, to dye, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁语 tingere（染色）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The word serves as noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼作名词与动词。

items.meaning: more than one; he or she does

definition_zh: 有活力的；动态的；不断变化的；动力学的
definition_en: full of energy and force, constantly changing or active, relating to motion and forces, or describing an action rather than a state
core_image: 一股看不见的力推着齿轮转动，整个系统都在变
scene: 创业公司的会议室里，白板写满又擦掉，讨论一直没停。She is a dynamic young manager who thrives on change.
sceneCN: 这里 dynamic 是「有活力的」（第 1 个义项：精力充沛、富有推动力）；句意是她是一位在变化中如鱼得水的有活力的年轻经理。

pos.zh: 形容词：有活力的；动态的；动力学的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -s 构成，义为「动力学；动态；力度变化」
由本词加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「动态地；有活力地」
由希腊词根 dynam- 加 -ism 构成，义为「活力；推动力」

senses.title: Full of energy
senses.definition: full of energy, new ideas and forcefulness, especially of a person or style
senses.definitionCN: 充满精力、新想法与推动力，尤用于人或风格
senses.example: She is a dynamic young manager who thrives on change.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位在变化中如鱼得水的有活力的年轻经理。
senses.why: Greek dynamis meant power, so a dynamic person is one who visibly carries power into whatever they do.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 dynamis 意为「力量」，所以 dynamic 的人就是明显把力量带进所做之事的人。

senses.title: Constantly changing
senses.definition: constantly changing, developing or moving, as a system, market or situation
senses.definitionCN: 不断变化、发展或运动，如系统、市场或局势
senses.example: The city has a dynamic economy that attracts young workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市拥有吸引年轻劳动者的充满活力的经济。
senses.why: A thing in motion cannot be captured in a single still picture, so dynamic marks whatever is still unfolding.
senses.whyCN: 运动中的事物无法被一张静止照片抓住，所以 dynamic 标记一切仍在展开的东西。

senses.title: Relating to forces in motion
senses.definition: relating to the forces that produce motion or change, used in physics and engineering
senses.definitionCN: 与产生运动或变化的力有关，用于物理与工程
senses.example: The engineers studied the dynamic loads on the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师研究了桥上的动态载荷。
senses.why: This is the technical home of the word: dynamis is power, and dynamics is the study of forces at work.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的技术归宿：dynamis 是力量，dynamics 就是研究运作中的力。

senses.title: Describing action, in grammar
senses.definition: describing an action or event rather than a state, as a dynamic verb does
senses.definitionCN: 描述动作或事件而非状态，如动态动词
senses.example: In this grammar, run is a dynamic verb and own is a stative one.
senses.exampleCN: 在这套语法里，run 是动态动词，own 是状态动词。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word to separate verbs that move from verbs that merely hold a state.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借用了这个词，用来把表示动作的动词与仅仅表示状态的动词分开。

intro.en: Dynamic comes from Greek dynamis, power, through the adjective dynamikos and later Latin and French forms.
intro.cn: dynamic 来自希腊语 dynamis（力量），经由形容词 dynamikos 以及后来的拉丁语、法语形式进入英语。

items.en: Greek dynamis meant power, strength or capacity, and it could also mean a force in nature.
items.cn: 希腊语 dynamis 意为「力量、能力」，也可指自然中的一种力。

items.en: The adjective dynamikos meant powerful or relating to force, and it was used in philosophy and science.
items.cn: 形容词 dynamikos 意为「有力的、与力有关的」，用于哲学与科学。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as dynamicus, keeping its learned and scientific tone.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词作 dynamicus，保留了学术与科学的语气。

items.en: French dynamique carried the word into modern European languages, including English.
items.cn: 法语 dynamique 把这个词带入包括英语在内的现代欧洲语言。

items.en: English dynamic is recorded in the nineteenth century, first in physics and then in general description.
items.cn: 英语 dynamic 在十九世纪有记录，先用于物理，再用于一般描述。

items.en: The word now describes lively people, changing markets and moving forces, all from one idea of power.
items.cn: 这个词如今描述有活力的人、变化的市场与运动中的力，全部来自同一个「力量」观念。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Greek power root; the near-meaning group separates energetic, active and vigorous by what kind of force they show.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊「力量」词根的词；近义组按所显现的力量类型区分 energetic、active 与 vigorous。

entries.definition: The study of forces and motion, or the pattern of forces in a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「动力学、动态」，指对力与运动的研究，或局势中的力量格局。

entries.definition: Great energy, drive or forcefulness in a person or system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「活力、推动力」，指人或系统中的巨大能量。

entries.definition: In a dynamic or energetic way; dynamic plus -ally.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「动态地、有活力地」，由 dynamic 加 -ally 构成。

entries.definition: An explosive; named from the same Greek word for power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「炸药」，由同一个表示「力量」的希腊词命名。

entries.definition: Full of physical or mental energy; it stresses activity rather than force.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精力充沛的」，强调活动而非力量。

entries.definition: Doing things, working or moving; neutral and broader than dynamic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活跃的、活动的」，中性且比 dynamic 更宽泛。

entries.definition: Strong, healthy and forceful in action; it stresses bodily strength.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强健有力的」，强调身体力量。

entries.definition: Not moving or changing; the direct opposite of the changing sense of dynamic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「静止的、静态的」，与 dynamic 的变化义正好相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks go back to Greek dynamis, power, and follow it into people, markets, physics and grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子回到希腊语 dynamis（力量），再跟着它走进人、市场、物理与语法。

normal.en: dynamis is power, so dynamic means carrying force.
normal.cn: dynamis 是力量，所以 dynamic 就是带着力量。

normal.en: A dynamic person moves things; a dynamic market keeps moving.
normal.cn: dynamic 的人能推动事情，dynamic 的市场一直在动。

normal.en: Dynamics is the science of those forces, and dynamism is the energy itself.
normal.cn: dynamics 是研究这些力的学问，dynamism 则是那股能量本身。

normal.en: Dynamic balance is balance kept while everything is moving.
normal.cn: dynamic balance 是在一切都在动的时候保持的平衡。

normal.en: A dynamic verb shows action, while a stative verb only holds a state.
normal.cn: 动态动词表示动作，状态动词只表示状态。

abstract.en: Picture a gear train turning with no visible hand behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一组齿轮在转动，背后却看不见任何手。

abstract.en: The same force can be drawn as a person pushing a project, or as a line on a physics diagram.
abstract.cn: 同一股力可以画成一个人推动项目，也可以画成物理图上的一个箭头。

abstract.en: Dynamic is power that refuses to stay still.
abstract.cn: dynamic 是不肯停下来的力量。

examples.en: She is a dynamic young manager who thrives on change.
examples.cn: 她是一位在变化中如鱼得水的有活力的年轻经理。

examples.en: The city has a dynamic economy that attracts young workers.
examples.cn: 这座城市拥有吸引年轻劳动者的充满活力的经济。

examples.en: The engineers studied the dynamic loads on the bridge.
examples.cn: 工程师研究了桥上的动态载荷。

dict_mnemonic.text: dynam- 是「力量」：dynamic 就是身上带力、局面在动、物理里研究力的那个词。

root: 来自希腊语 dynamis「力量、能力」，经形容词 dynamikos 进入拉丁语 dynamicus，再经法语 dynamique 进入英语，十九世纪先用于物理学。同族词有 dynamics、dynamism、dynamite。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of dynamic all carry one idea of power: in a person, in a changing system, in physical forces, and in verbs that show action.
sensesIntro.cn: dynamic 的四个义项都带着同一个「力量」观念：在人身上、在变化的系统中、在物理的力里，以及在表示动作的动词里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gear train turning under an invisible force.
core.cn: 核心意象：一组齿轮在一股看不见的力下转动。

branches.en: THE PERSON: energy that visibly pushes other people and projects.
branches.cn: 人物线：明显能推动他人与项目的能量。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a market or city that keeps changing shape.
branches.cn: 系统线：不断改变形态的市场或城市。

branches.en: THE PHYSICS: forces that produce motion, measured and diagrammed.
branches.cn: 物理线：产生运动的力，被测量并画成图。

branches.en: THE VERB: grammar separates actions from states with the same word.
branches.cn: 动词线：语法用同一个词把动作与状态分开。

branches.en: ONE FORCE AT THREE SCALES: a person, a market and a machine all carry power in motion.
branches.cn: 同一股力的三种尺度：人、市场与机器都在运动中带着力量。

intro.en: Dynamic is a Greek-derived adjective; English adds -s, -ally and -ism to make its family.
intro.cn: dynamic 是源自希腊语的形容词；英语加 -s、-ally、-ism 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek dynamis and dynamikos are recorded, and Latin dynamicus is attested as a learned borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 dynamis 与 dynamikos 均有记录，拉丁语 dynamicus 作为学术借词也有书证。

items.example: The root is shared by dynamics and dynamite.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为 dynamics 与 dynamite 所共用。

items.example: It is the source noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的源名词。

items.example: It is the direct model of dynamic.
items.exampleCN: 它是 dynamic 的直接原型。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -s 构成，义为「动力学；动态；力度变化」
由本词加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「动态地；有活力地」
由希腊词根 dynam- 加 -ism 构成，义为「活力；推动力」

definition_zh: 每个；各自的；每个地
definition_en: every one of two or more people or things, considered separately, used as a determiner, a pronoun or an adverb
core_image: 一排杯子被逐个拿起来查看，而不是整排一起看
scene: 老师把作业本一本本发下去，每个学生都拿到自己那份。Each student received a book.
sceneCN: 这里 each 是「每个」（第 1 个义项：把两个或以上的人或物逐个来看）；句意是每个学生都拿到了一本书。

pos.zh: 限定词：每个；各自的
代词：每个；各自
副词：每个；各

derivatives.zh: 由 each 与 other 组成的相互代词，义为「彼此；互相」
由 each 与 and every 组成的强调短语，义为「每一个，无一例外」
由 each 与 where 构成的古旧副词，义为「到处」

senses.title: Every one taken separately
senses.definition: every one of two or more people or things, thought of one by one rather than as a group
senses.definitionCN: 两个或以上的人或物中的每一个，逐个考虑而非作为整体
senses.example: Each student received a book.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都拿到了一本书。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase meaning ever alike, and it still treats the members one at a time, each alike in getting its own share.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是一个意为「永远相似」的短语，至今仍把成员一个一个看待，每个都一样地得到自己那份。

senses.title: Every one, as a pronoun
senses.definition: every one, used as a pronoun when the group has already been mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 每一个，在群体已被提及时用作代词
senses.example: Each of the rooms has its own key.
senses.exampleCN: 每个房间都有自己的钥匙。
senses.why: Once the group is known, the word can stand alone and still insist on one-by-one treatment.
senses.whyCN: 群体一旦已知，这个词就能独立使用，仍然坚持逐个看待。

senses.title: For every one
senses.definition: used before a number or amount to mean for every single one
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字或数量前，表示「每一个对应」
senses.example: The tickets cost ten dollars each.
senses.exampleCN: 这些票每张十美元。
senses.why: The adverb distributes a price or amount across members, keeping the same one-by-one count.
senses.whyCN: 副词把价格或数量分摊到每个成员身上，保持同样的逐个计数。

intro.en: Each goes back to Old English aelc, a contraction of a phrase meaning ever alike, with one member standing for the whole.
intro.cn: each 可追溯到古英语 aelc，是一个意为「永远相似」的短语缩合而成，用其中一个成员代表整体。

items.en: The form is reconstructed from two elements meaning ever and body or alike, giving the sense every one alike.
items.cn: 这个形式被重构为由「永远」与「身体、相似」两个成分组成，意为「每一个都相似」。

items.en: Old English aelc meant each or every, and it already required a singular verb and a singular noun.
items.cn: 古英语 aelc 意为「每个」，当时就已要求搭配单数动词和单数名词。

items.en: Middle English ech kept the one-by-one sense and simplified the spelling toward each.
items.cn: 中古英语 ech 保留逐个义，并把拼写简化到接近 each。

items.en: Each settled into its modern spelling and into the fixed pairs each other and each one.
items.cn: each 在十六世纪固定为现代拼写，并进入 each other、each one 等固定搭配。

items.en: The adverb use, as in ten dollars each, completed the word's modern range.
items.cn: 副词用法（如 ten dollars each）补齐了这个词的现代义域。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and phrases built on each; the near-meaning group separates every, all and any by how they group or separate members.
note.cn: 形近组收由 each 构成的短语与形式；近义组按如何聚合或分离成员区分 every、all 与 any。

entries.definition: A reciprocal pronoun meaning one another; each plus other.
entries.definitionCN: 相互代词，义为「彼此、互相」，由 each 加 other 构成。

entries.definition: A emphatic phrase meaning every single one without exception.
entries.definitionCN: 强调短语，义为「每一个，无一例外」。

entries.definition: Every single one, taken separately; a common emphatic form.
entries.definitionCN: 固定短语，义为「每一个」，逐个来看，是常见的强调形式。

entries.definition: All the members of a group, often treated as a whole rather than one by one.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「每个、所有」，常作为整体看待而非逐个。

entries.definition: All the individual members of a group, with less emphasis on separation than each.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「每一个」，与 each 相比较少强调分离。

entries.definition: The whole group together; it does not pick members out one by one.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词或代词，义为「全部」，把群体合在一起，不逐个挑出。

entries.definition: One or some, no matter which; used in questions and negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词或代词，义为「任何一个」，用于疑问和否定。

entries.definition: Each single member, written as two words when it means each individual.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「每一个」，表示逐个个体时写作两个词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the one-by-one picture and then place each beside every, all and any.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子守住逐个的画面，再把 each 与 every、all、any 放在一起比较。

normal.en: Each always looks at members one at a time, never as a crowd.
normal.cn: each 总是把成员一个一个看，从不当作一群人。

normal.en: Each takes a singular noun and a singular verb: each student is, not are.
normal.cn: each 搭配单数名词和单数动词：each student is，而不是 are。

normal.en: Each other is for two or more parties giving and receiving the same action.
normal.cn: each other 用于两方或多方互相给予、接受同一个动作。

normal.en: Each and every is the emphatic double, meaning not one is left out.
normal.cn: each and every 是强调性的叠加，意为一个也没漏掉。

normal.en: Ten dollars each distributes the price across every single buyer.
normal.cn: ten dollars each 把价格分摊到每一个买家身上。

abstract.en: Picture a row of cups, each lifted and checked before the next one.
abstract.cn: 想象一排杯子，每个都被拿起来检查过，才轮到下一个。

abstract.en: The same row seen from a distance becomes all; seen one by one it is each.
abstract.cn: 同一排从远处看是 all，逐个看就是 each。

abstract.en: Each is the word for counting members without losing any of them.
abstract.cn: each 是一个逐个计数却不漏掉任何成员的词。

examples.en: Each student received a book.
examples.cn: 每个学生都拿到了一本书。

examples.en: Each of the rooms has its own key.
examples.cn: 每个房间都有自己的钥匙。

examples.en: The tickets cost ten dollars each.
examples.cn: 这些票每张十美元。

dict_mnemonic.text: each 永远是一个一个地数：每个学生、每个房间、每张票，都不漏掉任何人。

root: 古英语 aelc「每个」，由意为「永远」与「相似、身体」的两个成分缩合而成，原意近于「每一个都相似」。中古英语作 ech，十六世纪固定为 each，并发展出 each other 与副词用法 ten dollars each。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of each all count members one by one: as a determiner, as a pronoun, and as an adverb distributing an amount.
sensesIntro.cn: each 的三个义项都在逐个计数成员：作限定词、作代词，以及作副词分摊数量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of cups, each lifted and examined in turn.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排杯子，每个都被依次拿起查看。

branches.en: THE DETERMINER: every member named separately before a singular noun.
branches.cn: 限定词线：在单数名词前逐个点名每一个成员。

branches.en: THE PRONOUN: the group is known and each member still stands alone.
branches.cn: 代词线：群体已知，每个成员仍单独站立。

branches.en: THE SHARE: a price or amount is handed out to every single one.
branches.cn: 份额线：价格或数量被发给每一个个体。

branches.en: NAME AND STAND-IN: the same one-by-one view works with or without a noun.
branches.cn: 点名与代称：同一种逐个视角，带不带名词都成立。

branches.en: COUNT AND DISTRIBUTE: each both picks members out and assigns their share.
branches.cn: 计数与分配：each 既挑出成员，也分配他们的一份。

intro.en: Each is a native pronoun-adjective; its family is made of fixed phrases rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: each 是本族语代词性形容词；它的词族主要由固定短语而非后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; Latin quisque, each one, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 quisque（每一个）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The word is the base of the family.
It is the historical shape of each.
items.exampleCN: 它是 each 的历史形态。

items.example: It appears in each and every.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 each and every 中。

items.example: It appears in each and every.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 each and every 中。

items.example: Each takes a singular verb ending.
items.exampleCN: each 搭配单数动词词尾。

definition_zh: 鹰；雕；鹰徽；鹰眼般的锐利目光；（高尔夫）老鹰球
definition_en: a large bird of prey with keen sight and powerful wings, a figure of such a bird used as an emblem, or a golf score of two strokes under par
core_image: 高空中展开双翼的猛禽，目光锁住地面上的猎物
scene: 山脊上的风把云推成一列，一只猛禽贴着上升气流盘旋。The eagle circled above the valley without a single beat of its wings.
sceneCN: 这里 eagle 是「鹰、雕」（第 1 个义项：目光锐利的大型猛禽）；句意为那只鹰一次翅膀都没扇，就在山谷上空盘旋。图中可辨识物件：山脊、上升气流、展开的双翼。

pos.zh: 名词：鹰、雕；鹰徽；老鹰球
动词：在高尔夫球中打出老鹰球

derivatives.zh: 由本词加指小后缀构成，义为「雏鹰」
由本词与 eyed 复合构成，义为「目光锐利的」

senses.title: A large bird of prey
senses.definition: a large strong bird that hunts smaller animals, with a hooked beak, sharp talons and very keen eyesight
senses.definitionCN: 捕食小型动物的大型强壮鸟类，有钩状的喙、尖利的爪和极敏锐的视力
senses.example: The eagle spotted a rabbit from a height of three hundred metres.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鹰从三百米高处发现了兔子。
senses.why: The Latin noun aquila named the bird first; the hooked beak and the far-seeing eye are the whole image behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 aquila 先给这种鸟命了名；钩状的喙与远望的眼睛就是这个词背后的全部意象。

senses.title: An emblem on flags and coins
senses.titleCN: 徽记：旗徽与币面上的鹰
senses.definition: a representation of an eagle used as a national, military or family emblem
senses.definitionCN: 用作国家、军队或家族标志的鹰的形象
senses.example: The coin carries an eagle on one side and a shield on the other.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚硬币一面是鹰，另一面是盾。
senses.why: Because the bird looks dominant and far-seeing, states put its picture on flags and coins to claim those same qualities.
senses.whyCN: 因为这鸟显得强势而远望，国家把它的形象印上旗帜与钱币，借以宣称自己也有这样的品质。

senses.title: Two strokes under par
senses.definition: a score of two strokes under par on a single hole
senses.definitionCN: 在单个球洞比标准杆少两杆的成绩
senses.example: She holed her second shot for an eagle on the par-five.
senses.exampleCN: 她在五杆洞第二杆直接入洞，打出老鹰球。
senses.why: Golf borrows bird names for scores below par, and the eagle ranks above the birdie because two under par is the rarer feat.
senses.whyCN: 高尔夫借用鸟名来称呼低于标准杆的成绩，老鹰球比小鸟球高一级，因为少两杆更罕见。

senses.title: The eagle eye
senses.definition: in the phrase eagle eye, an extremely keen ability to notice small details
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 eagle eye，指察觉细小事物时极敏锐的能力
senses.example: The inspector kept an eagle eye on every invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员以鹰一般的锐利目光盯着每一张发票。
senses.why: The bird's sight is the source of the idiom: to watch as an eagle watches is to miss nothing.
senses.whyCN: 这鸟的视力是这条习语的来源：像鹰那样看，就是什么都不漏。

intro.en: Eagle is a Latin borrowing that reached English through French, and its emblem sense was already present in Roman use.
intro.cn: eagle 是经由法语进入英语的拉丁语借词，徽记义在罗马时期就已存在。

items.en: A root for 'bird of prey' is sometimes reconstructed, but its exact shape and meaning are uncertain.
items.cn: 有时会重构一个表示「猛禽」的词根，但其确切形态与含义不确定。

items.en: Aquila was the ordinary Latin word for the eagle and also the name of the Roman military standard.
items.cn: aquila 是拉丁语中「鹰」的常用词，同时也是罗马军旗的名称。

items.en: Old French aigle came from the Latin form and carried both the bird and its heraldic use.
items.cn: 古法语 aigle 由拉丁语形式而来，同时带上「鸟」与纹章用法的含义。

items.en: Middle English used eagle beside older native names for the bird; the borrowed form eventually won out.
items.cn: 中古英语用 eagle，同时也用更早的本族词指这种鸟；借词形式最终胜出。

items.en: The golf sense is much later: sport borrowed the bird names to rank scores below par.
items.cn: 高尔夫义出现得晚得多：这项运动借用鸟名来给低于标准杆的成绩分等级。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same bird word; the near-meaning group gathers other raptors whose size and habits differ.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「鹰」词构成的形式；近义组收其他猛禽，体型与习性各有不同。

entries.definition: A young eagle, formed with a small noun suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 雏鹰，由本词加指小名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: An adjective describing someone who notices everything.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容人目光锐利、什么都不漏。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning eagle-like, especially of a hooked nose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「鹰一般的」，尤指钩形鼻。

entries.definition: A smaller daytime hunting bird with broad wings and a shorter beak.
entries.definitionCN: 一种体型较小的昼行猛禽，翼宽喙短。

entries.definition: A fast hunting bird with long pointed wings, often trained for falconry.
entries.definitionCN: 一种飞速快、翼长而尖的猎鸟，常被训练用于鹰猎。

normalIntro.en: These hooks climb from the bird on a thermal to the emblem, the golf score and the sharp eye.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从乘着上升气流盘旋的鸟，一路攀到徽记、高尔夫成绩与锐利目光。

normal.en: An eagle holds its wings still and lets rising air do the work.
normal.cn: 鹰把双翼展开不动，让上升的空气替它出力。

normal.en: The same bird sits on flags and coins because people want its reach and its stare.
normal.cn: 同一只鸟被放上旗帜与钱币，因为人们想要它的视野与凝视。

normal.en: Golf ranks birds by rarity, and two under par earns the eagle.
normal.cn: 高尔夫按罕见程度给鸟排名，少两杆才配得上老鹰。

normal.en: An eagle eye misses nothing, which is why inspectors are said to have one.
normal.cn: 鹰眼什么都不漏，所以人们说检查员长着一双鹰眼。

normal.en: Eagle and eaglet differ only in size, just as the words differ by one suffix.
normal.cn: eagle 与 eaglet 只差体型，两个词也只差一个后缀。

abstract.en: Picture a wide V of wings pinned above a valley, eyes locked on one moving dot.
abstract.cn: 想象山谷上方钉着一个宽大的 V 形双翼，眼睛死盯一个移动的小点。

abstract.en: The same V can be stitched on a flag, stamped on a coin or drawn on a scorecard.
abstract.cn: 同一个 V 形可以绣上旗帜、压进硬币，也可以画在记分卡上。

abstract.en: Eagle means height, command and unhurried sight, whichever object carries it.
abstract.cn: 无论载体是什么，eagle 都意味着高度、掌控与不急不躁的目力。

examples.en: The eagle nested on the cliff for more than a decade.
examples.cn: 那只鹰在悬崖上筑巢十多年了。

examples.en: A bald eagle appears on the back of the coin.
examples.cn: 硬币背面有一只白头鹰。

examples.en: He hit an eagle on the last hole and won by one stroke.
examples.cn: 他在最后一洞打出老鹰球，以一杆优势获胜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊格」——头顶一个钩喙，盘旋着盯住草地的兔子：鹰

root: 拉丁语 aquila「鹰」经由古法语 aigle 进入英语，aquila 同时是罗马军旗的名称。更早的印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of eagle all start from one bird: the animal itself, its use as a sign, a golf score named after it, and the keen gaze people borrow from it.
sensesIntro.cn: eagle 的四个义项都从同一只鸟出发：鸟本身、被当作标志的鸟、以它命名的老鹰球，以及人们从它借来的锐利目光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a great bird hangs on rising air, eyes fixed on a rabbit far below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只大鸟挂在上升的气流里，眼睛死盯下方很远处的一只兔子。

branches.en: THE BIRD: the animal itself, defined by hooked beak, talons and sight.
branches.cn: 鸟线：这种动物本身，以钩喙、利爪与视力为特征。

branches.en: THE SIGN: the bird's dominance is borrowed for flags, coins and family arms.
branches.cn: 标志线：人们借用这鸟的强势，把它放上旗帜、钱币与家族纹章。

branches.en: THE SCORE: sport takes the bird's name for a rare result under par.
branches.cn: 成绩线：运动借这鸟的名字，称呼低于标准杆的罕见成绩。

branches.en: THE GAZE: everyday speech takes the bird's sight as a model for noticing everything.
branches.cn: 目光线：日常语言把这鸟的视力当作「什么都不漏」的样板。

branches.en: THE EYE AUTHORITY: both the animal and the idiom rest on the same claim, that nothing escapes that stare.
branches.cn: 目力权威线：动物义与习语义都建立在同一个说法上——什么都逃不过那道凝视。

intro.en: Eagle is a Latin borrowing through French, so English adds only small suffixes and compounds to the borrowed stem.
intro.cn: eagle 是经由法语而来的拉丁语借词，英语只在借来的词干上加小后缀与复合成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin aquila and its use for the military standard are recorded; only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aquila 及其军旗用法均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧语词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The noun already joined the bird and the standard.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词已经把「鸟」与「军旗」合在一起。
这个词根出现在 aquiline 里。

items.meaning: having eyes of a stated kind

items.example: The phrase works as a fixed idiom.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语作为固定习语使用。

items.example: The compound names one particular species.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词专指一个物种。

definition_zh: 耳朵；听力；辨音力；（麦、玉米等的）穗；倾听
definition_en: the organ of hearing, the ability to hear and judge sound, or the head of a grain plant; also the attention given to what someone says
core_image: 贴在头侧的一只耳朵，把空气里的振动收进颅内
scene: 谷仓边的风把麦浪吹得沙沙响，老人停下脚步侧过头去听。She cupped a hand behind her ear to catch the whisper.
sceneCN: 这里 ear 是「耳朵」（第 1 个义项：听觉器官）；句意为她把手罩在耳后，好接住那句低语。图中可辨识物件：麦浪、谷仓、耳廓。

pos.zh: 名词：耳朵；听力；辨音力；穗

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 drum 复合构成，义为「鼓膜」
由本词与 lobe 复合构成，义为「耳垂」
由本词与 ring 复合构成，义为「耳环」
由本词与 ache 复合构成，义为「耳痛」

senses.title: The organ of hearing
senses.definition: the part of the body on the side of the head that receives sound and sends it to the brain
senses.definitionCN: 头部两侧接收声音并把它传向大脑的身体部位
senses.example: The sound entered one ear and seemed to stop there.
senses.exampleCN: 那声音进入一只耳朵，似乎就停在那里了。
senses.why: Old English eare named the body part long before any metaphor; the ear is simply the opening through which sound is taken in.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 eare 早于一切比喻就给这个身体部位命名；耳朵就是声音被收进来的那个开口。

senses.title: The ability to judge sound
senses.titleCN: 辨音力：对声音的判断力
senses.definition: the ability to hear and distinguish sounds, especially musical ones, accurately
senses.definitionCN: 准确听辨声音、尤其是音乐的能力
senses.example: She has a good ear for accents.
senses.exampleCN: 她对口音有很好的辨音力。
senses.why: What the organ does well becomes the name of the skill: a good ear is an ear that judges what it hears.
senses.whyCN: 器官做得好的事就成了技能的名字：a good ear 就是一只会判断所听之声的耳朵。

senses.title: The head of a grain plant
senses.definition: the part of a plant such as wheat or maize that holds the grains
senses.definitionCN: 小麦、玉米等植物承载谷粒的部分
senses.example: An ear of wheat lay across the threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 一穗小麦横在门槛上。
senses.why: This is a different Old English word that happened to be spelled the same; the grain head was never derived from hearing.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个古英语词，只是碰巧拼写相同；谷物穗头与「听」的义项从无派生关系。

senses.title: Attention given to a speaker
senses.titleCN: 倾听：给予说话者的注意
senses.definition: in phrases such as lend an ear, the act of listening attentively to someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于 lend an ear 等短语，指认真听别人说话的行为
senses.example: The boy lent an ear to his grandfather's story.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩认真听祖父讲故事。
senses.why: Listening is what the ear is for, so lending an ear became the idiom for giving someone your attention.
senses.whyCN: 听正是耳朵的用途，于是 lend an ear 就成了「把注意力给某人」的习语。

intro.en: English ear is two different words that fell together in spelling: the hearing organ and the grain head have separate Old English origins.
intro.cn: 英语 ear 其实是两个不同的词在拼写上合并了：听觉器官与谷物穗头各有独立的古英语来源。

items.en: The hearing word goes back to a root widely reconstructed as 'ear', though the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 表示「听」的词可追溯到通常重构为「耳」的词根，但其确切形态不确定。

items.en: Eare named the organ of hearing and is the direct source of modern ear.
items.cn: eare 指听觉器官，是现代 ear 的直接来源。

items.en: A separate noun ear meant the head of grain; it is unrelated to the hearing word.
items.cn: 另有一个名词 ear 意为谷物穗头，与表示「听」的词并无亲缘关系。

items.en: The two nouns came to share one spelling, and only context tells them apart.
items.cn: 两个名词逐渐共用一种拼写，只能靠上下文区分。

items.en: Musical and conversational idioms grew from the hearing sense, while farming kept the grain sense alive.
items.cn: 音乐与谈话类习语从「听」的义项长出，农业则让「穗」的义项继续存活。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that merely resemble ear in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for hearing and listening.
note.cn: 形近组收只是在拼写上像 ear 的词；近义组收表示「听」与「倾听」的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to gain money or respect through work, with no link to hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为靠劳动挣得钱财或赢得尊重，与「听」无关。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning before the usual time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼副词，义为「早的、提早的」。

entries.definition: The membrane inside the ear that vibrates with sound.
entries.definitionCN: 耳内随声音振动的薄膜，即鼓膜。

entries.definition: The ability or act of perceiving sound.
entries.definitionCN: 感知声音的能力或行为。

entries.definition: The act of paying attention to sound or speech.
entries.definitionCN: 注意听声音或言语的行为。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the hearing ear and the grain ear apart, then add the idioms that grew from listening.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子先把「听的耳朵」与「谷物的穗」分开，再补上从「听」长出的习语。

normal.en: Move one letter and ear becomes hear: the organ is named for what it does.
normal.cn: 挪一个字母，ear 就成了 hear：这个器官是按它的功能命名的。

normal.en: An ear for music is not a body part but a skill the body part makes possible.
normal.cn: an ear for music 不是身体部位，而是这个部位使人具备的技能。

normal.en: The ear of wheat is a namesake only; the grain never listened to anything.
normal.cn: 麦穗的 ear 只是同名而已，谷物从不听任何声音。

normal.en: To lend an ear is to hand over your attention for a while.
normal.cn: lend an ear 就是把你的注意力借出去一会儿。

normal.en: Playing it by ear means following the music without a score, then following events without a plan.
normal.cn: play it by ear 原指不看谱、跟着音乐走，后来指没有计划、跟着事情走。

abstract.en: Picture a small open shell on the side of a head, catching ripples from the air.
abstract.cn: 想象头侧一只敞开的小贝壳，接住从空气里传来的波纹。

abstract.en: The same shell can be a listener, a judge of pitch, or a handle for an idiom about attention.
abstract.cn: 同一只贝壳可以是听者、音高判断者，也可以是一条关于注意力的习语的把手。

abstract.en: Ear means reception: whatever comes in through that opening, sound, music or a story.
abstract.cn: ear 意味着接收：凡是从那个开口进来的东西，声音、音乐或一个故事。

examples.en: The sound entered one ear and seemed to stop there.
examples.cn: 那声音进入一只耳朵，似乎就停在那里了。

examples.en: She has a good ear for accents.
examples.cn: 她对口音有很好的辨音力。

examples.en: An ear of wheat lay across the threshold.
examples.cn: 一穗小麦横在门槛上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊尔」——侧过头，把声音兜进那只小贝壳

root: 表示「耳朵」的 ear 来自古英语 eare，可上溯到通常重构为「耳」的印欧词根；表示「穗」的 ear 来自另一个古英语词 ear，二者仅拼写相同。更早形态不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of ear cover two unrelated nouns and two extensions: the hearing organ, the skill it enables, the grain head that shares its spelling, and the act of listening.
sensesIntro.cn: ear 的四个义项包含两个无关名词与两重引申：听觉器官、它带来的辨音技能、共用拼写的谷物穗头，以及倾听的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small open shell on the side of a head catches a ripple of air.
core.cn: 核心意象：头侧一只敞开的小贝壳接住空气的波纹。

branches.en: THE ORGAN: the physical ear, the opening that takes sound in.
branches.cn: 器官线：物理的耳朵，把声音收进来的那个开口。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: what the organ does well becomes a name for the skill of judging sound.
branches.cn: 判断线：器官做得好的事，成了判断声音这项技能的名字。

branches.en: THE PLANT: a separate noun with the same spelling, naming the head that holds grain.
branches.cn: 植物线：一个拼写相同的独立名词，指承载谷粒的穗头。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: lending an ear turns the organ into an act of attention.
branches.cn: 动作线：lend an ear 把这个器官变成一种给予注意的行为。

branches.en: THE RECEIVER: organ, skill and gesture all describe something coming in through the same opening.
branches.cn: 接收线：器官、技能与动作都在描述同一种东西从那个开口进来。

intro.en: Ear is a native Old English noun; English expands it mainly by compounding and a few ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: ear 是古英语本族名词，英语主要靠复合与少量普通后缀来扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Latin auris is the recorded source of the learned adjectives, while the everyday noun remains Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 auris 是相关书面形容词的可考来源，而日常名词仍属日耳曼语族。

items.example: It is the direct source of modern ear.
items.exampleCN: 它是现代 ear 的直接来源。

items.example: This noun is unrelated to hearing.
The Latin noun supplies learned adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词提供了一些书面形容词。

definition_zh: 早的；提早的；早期的；清晨的；过早地
definition_en: happening before the usual or expected time, or near the beginning of a period
core_image: 天还没亮，集市上已经有人摆好第一筐菜
scene: 天光只露一线，街口的早点摊已经冒起白汽。A farmer arrives early to claim the corner stall.
sceneCN: 这里 early 是「早、提早」（第 1 个义项：比通常时间更早）；句意为农夫早早赶到，占下街角的摊位。图中可辨识物件：天光、早点摊、菜筐。

pos.zh: 形容词：早的；提早的；早期的；清晨的
副词：早；提早；在初期

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「早；提前」
由本词与 bird 复合构成，义为「早起的人」

senses.title: Before the expected time
senses.titleCN: 提前的：比预期时间更早
senses.definition: happening or arriving before the usual or expected time
senses.definitionCN: 在通常或预期的时间之前发生或到达
senses.example: The train left five minutes early.
senses.exampleCN: 火车提前五分钟开走了。
senses.why: Old English ǣr meant 'before', and the whole word is that idea carried into an adjective and an adverb.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ǣr 意为「在……之前」，整个词就是把这个意思搬进形容词与副词。

senses.title: Near the beginning of a period
senses.titleCN: 早期的：一段时间的前段
senses.definition: belonging to the first part of a period, process or history
senses.definitionCN: 属于一段时间、过程或历史的前段
senses.example: Early settlers built their huts along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 早期定居者沿河搭起了小屋。
senses.why: A period is imagined as a line with a start; whatever sits near that start is early in it.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间被想象成一条有起点的线；靠近起点的事物就在这段时间的早期。

senses.title: In the first hours of the day
senses.titleCN: 清晨的：一天的最初时段
senses.definition: in the first part of the morning, before most activity begins
senses.definitionCN: 在上午的前段，多数活动尚未开始之时
senses.example: He wakes early even on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 他连星期天也醒得很早。
senses.why: The day is the most familiar period of all, so early most often means before the day has properly started.
senses.whyCN: 一天是最熟悉的一段时间，所以 early 最常指一天尚未真正开始之前。

senses.title: Too soon
senses.definition: happening before the proper or suitable moment, so that a judgement or action is premature
senses.definitionCN: 在恰当或合适的时刻之前发生，使判断或行动显得为时过早
senses.example: It is too early to tell whether the plan will work.
senses.exampleCN: 现在判断这个计划是否行得通还为时过早。
senses.why: Once 'before the time' is applied to what should have waited, early turns into a criticism: too soon.
senses.whyCN: 当「在时间之前」被用到本该再等等的事情上，early 就变成一种批评：太早了。

intro.en: Early is a native English word built from an Old English adverb meaning 'before' plus the ordinary -ly ending.
intro.cn: early 是英语本族词，由古英语中意为「在……之前」的副词加普通 -ly 词尾构成。

items.en: A Germanic form meaning 'early, soon' is reconstructed, but its precise shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个意为「早、不久」的日耳曼语形式，但其确切形态不确定。

items.en: The adverb ǣr meant 'before, earlier, soon' and is the core of the word.
items.cn: 副词 ǣr 意为「之前、更早、不久」，是整个词的核心。

items.en: Ǣr plus the ending -līce produced an adverb meaning 'early'.
items.cn: ǣr 加上词尾 -līce 构成了意为「早地」的副词。

items.en: The form shortened in spelling, and the word began to work as an adjective as well as an adverb.
items.cn: 这个词的拼写缩短了，并开始兼作形容词与副词。

items.en: The adjective use is established by the fourteenth century, though the exact dating is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词用法在十四世纪已确立，但确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the opening letters; the near-meaning group gathers words for what happens before time or too soon.
note.cn: 形近组收开头字母相同的词；近义组收表示「在时间之前」或「过早」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为靠努力挣得钱财或赢得尊重。

entries.definition: The organ of hearing, or the head of a grain plant.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉器官，或谷物的穗头。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning serious and sincere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「认真的、诚挚的」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a short time from now, or before the expected time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不久、很快」，也可指早于预期。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning happening before the proper or usual time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过早的、时机未到的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the clock to the calendar, then to the light of morning and the warning that it is too soon.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从钟表走到日历，再走到清晨的光，最后到「时候未到」的警告。

normal.en: Early is a clock word first: the hand has not reached the agreed mark.
normal.cn: early 首先是钟表词：指针还没走到约定的刻度。

normal.en: Stretch the clock into a calendar and early means the first pages of a history.
normal.cn: 把钟表拉成日历，early 就指一段历史最前面的几页。

normal.en: The day is the period everyone shares, so early usually means before sunrise activity.
normal.cn: 一天是人人共用的一段时间，所以 early 通常指日出活动之前。

normal.en: Say too early and the same word turns from praise into caution.
normal.cn: 加上 too，同一个词就从称赞变成提醒。

normal.en: An early bird catches the worm because it acts before the crowd.
normal.cn: 早起的鸟能吃到虫，因为它赶在人群之前行动。

abstract.en: Picture a finish line whose tape is still far away, while a runner is already through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条终点线，带子还在远处，跑者却已经冲了过去。

abstract.en: The same gap before the mark can be a train, a century or a single morning.
abstract.cn: 刻度之前的那段距离，可以是一列火车、一个世纪，也可以是一个清晨。

abstract.en: Early means ahead of the expected position on some line of time.
abstract.cn: early 意味着在某条时间线上，走到了预期位置之前。

examples.en: The train left five minutes early.
examples.cn: 火车提前五分钟开走了。

examples.en: Early settlers built their huts along the river.
examples.cn: 早期定居者沿河搭起了小屋。

examples.en: He wakes early even on Sundays.
examples.cn: 他连星期天也醒得很早。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄立」——天没亮，摊子已经摆好第一筐菜

root: 古英语副词 ǣr「之前、更早」加词尾 -līce 构成 ǣrlīce，后缩为 early；其日耳曼语来源形态不确定，更早的印欧语来源亦不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of early all place something before a mark: before the hour, before the middle of a period, before the day's activity, or before the right moment.
sensesIntro.cn: early 的四个义项都在把某物放到某个刻度之前：钟点之前、一段时间的中段之前、一天的活动之前，或恰当时机之前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner breaks the tape while the clock still shows time to spare.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑者冲过终点带时，时钟上还留着余量。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the hand arrives before the agreed mark.
branches.cn: 钟表线：指针在约定的刻度之前到达。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: the same gap stretched over years becomes the first part of a history.
branches.cn: 日历线：同一段距离拉长到多年，就成了历史的前段。

branches.en: THE MORNING: the day is the shared period, so early settles on the hours before activity.
branches.cn: 清晨线：一天是共用的一段时间，early 便落在活动开始前的那几个小时。

branches.en: THE WARNING: applied to what should have waited, before the time becomes too soon.
branches.cn: 警告线：用在理应再等等的事情上，「在时间之前」就变成了「太早」。

branches.en: THE DAILY RACE: the clock sense and the morning sense meet in the early bird hurrying out.
branches.cn: 日常竞速线：钟表义与清晨义在匆匆出门的 early bird 身上汇合。

intro.en: Early is a native compound of an Old English adverb and a suffix; later English adds only a noun ending and a fixed compound.
intro.cn: early 是古英语副词与后缀构成的本族复合词，后来的英语只加了一个名词词尾与一个固定复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the word belongs to the Germanic layer of English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，属于英语的日耳曼语层。

items.example: The adverb supplies the meaning of beforeness.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词提供「在前」的核心含义。

items.example: It turned the adverb into a fuller form.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个副词变成更完整的形式。

items.example: This is the direct ancestor of early.
items.exampleCN: 这是 early 的直接祖先。

items.example: The modern ending continues the old suffix.
items.exampleCN: 现代词尾延续了古后缀。

definition_zh: 挣得；赚得；赢得；博得；生（利息）
definition_en: to get money or something else of value in return for work or effort, or to gain a quality such as respect because one deserves it
core_image: 汗湿的手把一天的工钱攥紧，钱是自己挣来的
scene: 砖窑的日头落下去，工人领到当天的工钱。Two weeks of night shifts earned him enough for the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 earn 是「挣得（钱）」（第 1 个义项：靠劳动换取报酬）；句意为两周夜班让他挣够了房租。图中可辨识物件：砖窑、工钱、落日。

pos.zh: 动词：挣得；赚得；赢得；博得；生（利息）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「收入；收益」
由本词加施事后缀构成，义为「挣钱者；收入来源」
由否定前缀与本词加后缀构成，义为「非劳动所得的」

senses.title: To get money by working
senses.definition: to receive money in return for work or services
senses.definitionCN: 因工作或服务而获得钱财
senses.example: She earns more in a week than her father did in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她一周挣得比她父亲当年一个月挣得还多。
senses.why: Old English earnian already meant to earn wages; money is what the work is exchanged for.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 earnian 已经表示「挣得工钱」；钱就是劳动所换来的东西。

senses.title: To gain something by merit
senses.definition: to gain a quality such as respect, trust or a place because one deserves it
senses.definitionCN: 因自己配得上而获得尊重、信任或某个位置等
senses.example: He earned the trust of every farmer in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢得了山谷里每一位农夫的信任。
senses.why: The same verb moves from wages to worth: effort and character are the labour that earns trust or respect.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从工钱移到价值：努力与品格就是挣得信任或尊重的劳动。

senses.title: To yield as interest or profit
senses.definition: to produce interest or profit, said of money that is saved or invested
senses.definitionCN: 指被存下或投入的钱产生利息或利润
senses.example: The account earns four percent interest each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个账户每年生百分之四的利息。
senses.why: Money set aside is imagined as working on your behalf, so it too earns something for you.
senses.whyCN: 存起来的钱被想象成替你干活，于是它也能为你挣得些什么。

intro.en: Earn is native Old English, and its earliest sense was closer to 'deserve' than to 'take home a wage'.
intro.cn: earn 是古英语本族词，最早的含义更接近「应得」，而不是「领回工资」。

items.en: A wider origin beyond Germanic is often proposed but not settled, so it is best treated as uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼语之外的更早来源常有推测，但尚无定论，宜视为不确定。

items.en: A Germanic verb with the sense of earning or deserving is reconstructed from the related forms.
items.cn: 根据相关形式可重构出一个表示「挣得、应得」的日耳曼语动词。

items.en: Earnian meant to earn, deserve or merit something through effort.
items.cn: earnian 意为靠努力挣得、应得或配得上某物。

items.en: The verb narrowed toward wages and money while the merit sense survived in phrases.
items.cn: 这个动词向「工钱、钱财」收窄，而「应得」的意思在短语里留存下来。

items.en: Earn respect and earn interest show the old merit sense and the newer financial sense side by side.
items.cn: earn respect 与 earn interest 并列展示出较旧的「应得」义与较新的财务义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that sound or look close but mean something else; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for getting value.
note.cn: 形近组收读音或拼写接近但意思不同的词；近义组收表示「取得价值」的动词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to long for something strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「渴望、向往」。

entries.definition: The organ of hearing, or the head of a grain plant.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉器官，或谷物的穗头。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning before the usual time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼副词，义为「早的、提早的」。

entries.definition: To obtain something, often through effort or over time.
entries.definitionCN: 获得某物，常指经努力或随时间而来。

entries.definition: To be worthy of something because of one's actions or qualities.
entries.definitionCN: 因行为或品质而配得上某物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the word from wages to trust, then to money that works on its own.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着这个词从工钱走到信任，再走到自己会干活的钱。

normal.en: Earn begins as 'deserve', then settles on 'take home pay'.
normal.cn: earn 起初是「应得」，后来落在「领回家的钱」上。

normal.en: Work is exchanged for money, which is the plainest kind of earning.
normal.cn: 劳动换来钱财，这是最直白的一种挣得。

normal.en: Trust and respect are wages paid in another currency.
normal.cn: 信任与尊重是用另一种货币支付的工钱。

normal.en: Money in a savings account is said to earn because it is imagined as working.
normal.cn: 储蓄账户里的钱被说成 earn，因为它被想象成在干活。

normal.en: Keep yearn apart: one word stretches toward what is absent, the other collects what is due.
normal.cn: 把 yearn 分清楚：一个词伸向缺席之物，另一个词收下应得之物。

abstract.en: Picture a coin weighed on one side by hours of work and on the other by a printed wage.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币，一边压着数小时劳动，一边压着印好的工资数。

abstract.en: The same scales can weigh trust, a place at a table, or interest on a deposit.
abstract.cn: 同一架天平也能称信任、桌上的一席之位，或存款的利息。

abstract.en: Earn means the balance was paid for, not simply received.
abstract.cn: earn 意味着这份平衡是付过代价换来的，而不是白得的。

examples.en: She earns more in a week than her father did in a month.
examples.cn: 她一周挣得比她父亲当年一个月挣得还多。

examples.en: He earned the trust of every farmer in the valley.
examples.cn: 他赢得了山谷里每一位农夫的信任。

examples.en: The account earns four percent interest each year.
examples.cn: 这个账户每年生百分之四的利息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄恩」——夜里搬砖，天亮攥住自己换来的钱

root: 古英语 earnian「应得、挣得」来自日耳曼语层，同族形式在德语与荷兰语中表示收获或劳作报酬；日耳曼语之外的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of earn all describe value obtained because something was given first: labour for money, effort for trust, and savings for interest.
sensesIntro.cn: earn 的三个义项都在描述「先付出、后取得」的价值：劳动换钱、努力换信任、存款换利息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin is weighed against hours of work, and the two sides come level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币与数小时劳动放在天平两端，最后持平。

branches.en: THE WAGE: hours of work are exchanged for money.
branches.cn: 工钱线：数小时劳动被换成钱财。

branches.en: THE MERIT: effort and character are exchanged for trust or respect.
branches.cn: 功绩线：努力与品格被换成信任或尊重。

branches.en: THE YIELD: saved money is imagined as working and returning interest.
branches.cn: 收益线：存下的钱被想象成在干活，并带回利息。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: in both cases something must be given before the gain is paid out.
branches.cn: 条件线：两种情况下都得先付出，收获才会被支付。

branches.en: THE RETURN: what comes back is proportional to what was put in, whether labour or capital.
branches.cn: 回报线：回来的东西与投入的东西相称，无论投入的是劳动还是资本。

intro.en: Earn is a native Germanic verb; English adds ordinary suffixes and one negative prefix, plus a few fixed phrases.
intro.cn: earn 是日耳曼语本族动词，英语加上普通后缀、一个否定前缀，以及若干固定短语。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is involved; the related forms belong to the Germanic languages.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁语来源，相关形式属于日耳曼语族。

items.example: The Old English verb already joined pay and merit.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词已经把「报酬」与「应得」合在一起。

items.example: The form is reconstructed, not recorded.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式是重构的，并非有记录的原词。

definition_zh: 认真的；诚挚的；坚决的；定金；保证
definition_en: serious and sincere in intention, not joking; also a sum of money paid as a pledge
core_image: 年轻人把简历放正，坐得笔直，一句玩笑也不说
scene: 年轻人把简历放在桌上，坐得笔直，等对方先开口。He gave an earnest answer to every question.
sceneCN: 这里 earnest 是「认真的、诚挚的」（第 1 个义项：态度严肃而真诚）；句意为他对每个问题都作了认真的回答。图中可辨识物件：简历、桌面、挺直的坐姿。

pos.zh: 形容词：认真的；诚挚的；坚决的
名词：定金；保证

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「认真地；诚挚地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「认真；诚挚」

senses.title: Serious and sincere
senses.titleCN: 认真的：态度严肃而真诚
senses.definition: serious in what one says or does, and sincere rather than playful
senses.definitionCN: 言行严肃，出于真诚而非玩笑
senses.example: He gave an earnest answer to every question.
senses.exampleCN: 他对每个问题都作了认真的回答。
senses.why: Old English eornost named seriousness of purpose, and the adjective kept that plain face-to-face honesty.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 eornost 指目的上的严肃，形容词保留的就是这种面对面的坦率真诚。

senses.title: Determined in purpose
senses.definition: showing deep commitment to a goal, so that one will not be easily turned aside
senses.definitionCN: 对目标表现出深切的投入，不轻易被改变
senses.example: She made an earnest attempt to learn the trade from the ground up.
senses.exampleCN: 她下定决心，要从头学起这门手艺。
senses.why: The same seriousness deepens into resolve: what is taken earnestly is pursued to the end.
senses.whyCN: 同一种严肃会加深为决心：被认真对待的事，就会被追到底。

senses.title: In earnest: seriously, for real
senses.definition: in the phrase in earnest, in a serious manner or with real intent, not as a trial
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in earnest，表示以严肃的方式或带着真实意图，而非试试看
senses.example: The rain began in earnest just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜刚过，雨就真正下起来了。
senses.why: The phrase marks the moment when pretence stops and the thing is done for real.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语标出假装结束、事情开始动真格的那一刻。

senses.title: A pledge paid in advance
senses.definition: a sum of money paid to bind an agreement, often called earnest money
senses.definitionCN: 为约束一项协议而支付的一笔钱，常称 earnest money
senses.example: The buyer put down earnest money to hold the house.
senses.exampleCN: 买方付了定金，把房子留住。
senses.why: A pledge is seriousness made visible; this noun sense may have a separate origin, and the sources do not fully agree.
senses.whyCN: 保证就是把「认真」变成看得见的东西；这个名词义可能有独立来源，各家说法并不完全一致。

intro.en: Earnest is a native English word for seriousness, and its noun sense of a pledge may come from a different route.
intro.cn: earnest 是英语本族中表示「认真」的词，而「定金」的名词义可能来自另一条路径。

items.en: A Germanic noun for zeal or seriousness is reconstructed behind the Old English form, but its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 古英语形式背后可重构出一个表示「热忱、严肃」的日耳曼语名词，但其确切形态不确定。

items.en: Eornost meant seriousness, zeal or earnestness, and also gave the adjective.
items.cn: eornost 意为严肃、热忱、认真，同时也派生出形容词。

items.en: The adjective settled into the modern spelling earnest and kept both the sincere and the resolute senses.
items.cn: 形容词固定为现代拼写 earnest，并保留了「真诚」与「坚决」两义。

items.en: Earnest money became a fixed term in contracts; some sources link this noun to a different Old French form, and the question is unsettled.
items.cn: earnest money 成为合同中的固定术语；有些资料把这个名词联系到另一个古法语形式，此问题尚无定论。

items.en: In everyday use the adjective outweighs the noun, while in earnest remains one of the commonest phrases.
items.cn: 在现代日常用法中形容词远多于名词，而 in earnest 仍是最常见的短语之一。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the opening sound; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for seriousness and sincerity.
note.cn: 形近组收开头读音相同的词；近义组收表示「严肃」与「真诚」的形容词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to gain money or respect through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为靠努力挣得钱财或赢得尊重。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning before the usual time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼副词，义为「早的、提早的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being serious and sincere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指认真而诚挚的品质。

entries.definition: Free from pretence, saying honestly what one feels.
entries.definitionCN: 不装假，如实说出所感。

entries.definition: Not joking, and treating a matter as important.
entries.definitionCN: 不开玩笑，把事情当作重要的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a straight-backed posture to a promise backed by money.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从挺直的坐姿，走到用钱作保的承诺。

normal.en: Earnest is a posture before it is a word: no joke in the face, no slouch in the chair.
normal.cn: earnest 先是一种姿态，然后才是一个词：脸上没有玩笑，椅子上没有瘫坐。

normal.en: Seriousness that lasts becomes resolve, and resolve is the second sense.
normal.cn: 持续的认真会变成决心，而决心就是第二个义项。

normal.en: In earnest marks the line between pretending and really doing it.
normal.cn: in earnest 标出「假装」与「真做」之间的那条线。

normal.en: Earnest money turns a spoken promise into something the buyer can lose.
normal.cn: earnest money 把口头承诺变成买方可能损失的东西。

normal.en: Earnest and earn open alike but part ways: one is owed money, the other is meant seriously.
normal.cn: earnest 与 earn 开头相似却分道扬镳：一个是被挣的钱，一个是认真的心意。

abstract.en: Picture a signature made slowly, with the pen pressed hard enough to leave a groove.
abstract.cn: 想象一个慢慢写下的签名，笔压得足够重，留下了凹痕。

abstract.en: The same pressure can appear as a straight back, a promise, or a deposit on a house.
abstract.cn: 同一股力道可以表现为挺直的背、一句承诺，或一套房子的定金。

abstract.en: Earnest means nothing here is being held back or played with.
abstract.cn: earnest 意味着这里没有任何东西被保留或被拿来玩。

examples.en: He gave an earnest answer to every question.
examples.cn: 他对每个问题都作了认真的回答。

examples.en: She made an earnest attempt to learn the trade from the ground up.
examples.cn: 她下定决心，要从头学起这门手艺。

examples.en: The buyer put down earnest money to hold the house.
examples.cn: 买方付了定金，把房子留住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄尼斯特」——坐得笔直，一句玩笑都不说

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of earnest run from a sincere face to a resolute purpose, the phrase in earnest, and a pledge paid in money.
sensesIntro.cn: earnest 的四个义项从真诚的神色，走到坚决的目的、短语 in earnest，再到以钱支付的保证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature is pressed slowly into paper, leaving a groove behind the pen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个签名被慢慢压进纸里，笔后留下凹痕。

branches.en: THE FACE: the plain, unplayful manner of someone who means what is said.
branches.cn: 神色线：一个说到做到的人那种平实、不开玩笑的态度。

branches.en: THE PURPOSE: seriousness held over time hardens into resolve.
branches.cn: 目的线：持续一段时间的认真会硬化成决心。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: in earnest marks the switch from rehearsal to the real thing.
branches.cn: 短语线：in earnest 标出从演练切换到真事的那一刻。

branches.en: THE PLEDGE: money makes the promise tangible and costly to break.
branches.cn: 保证线：钱让承诺变得可触，也让毁约变得有代价。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: face, resolve and deposit all show seriousness that will not be taken back.
branches.cn: 分量线：神色、决心与定金都在显示一种不会收回的认真。

intro.en: Earnest is a native stem; English adds two common suffixes and fixed phrases rather than Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: earnest 是本族词干，英语给它加的是两个普通后缀与固定短语，而非拉丁语前缀。

latinIntro.en: The adjective has no Latin source; the commercial noun may have passed through French, but that link is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 形容词没有拉丁语来源；商业名词义可能经法语而来，但这一联系不确定。

items.example: The noun is the base of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是现代词的基底。

items.example: It forms a rare comparative of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成该形容词罕见的比较级。

definition_en: the planet we live on, the soil or ground beneath us, dry land as opposed to sea, or the human world
core_image: 掌心里一捧湿土，抬头却是一整颗蓝白的球
scene: 从月面回望，一颗蓝白相间的球悬在黑暗里。The earth turned slowly beneath the station's window.
sceneCN: 这里 earth 是「地球」（第 1 个义项：我们居住的行星）；句意为地球在空间站窗下缓缓转动。图中可辨识物件：月面、蓝色星球、舷窗。

pos.zh: 名词：地球；泥土；地面；陆地；人间
动词：把（电线）接地

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「泥土般的；朴实的」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「土制的；陶制的」

senses.title: The planet we live on
senses.definition: the planet that orbits the sun and is the home of human beings
senses.definitionCN: 绕太阳运行、人类赖以生存的行星
senses.example: The earth turned slowly beneath the station's window.
senses.exampleCN: 地球在空间站窗下缓缓转动。
senses.why: The oldest sense was the ground beneath the feet; the planet took the same name once people saw it as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是脚下的地面；当人们把行星看成一个整体，它就沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: Soil and ground
senses.definition: the substance of the ground, especially the soil in which plants grow
senses.definitionCN: 地面的物质，尤指植物生长的土壤
senses.example: She pressed a handful of earth around the seedling.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一把土按在幼苗周围。
senses.why: This is the word at its most concrete: what can be dug, carried and held in one hand.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最具体的用法：能被挖起、搬走、握在一只手里的东西。

senses.title: Dry land
senses.definition: the surface of the planet that is not covered by water
senses.definitionCN: 行星表面未被水覆盖的部分
senses.example: After weeks at sea, the sailors sighted earth.
senses.exampleCN: 在海上漂了几周后，水手们看见了陆地。
senses.why: For travellers the useful contrast is water and not water, so earth came to mean the dry half of the surface.
senses.whyCN: 对旅人来说，有用的对比是「水」与「非水」，于是 earth 指表面干燥的那一半。

senses.title: The human world
senses.definition: the world of human life and affairs, often as opposed to heaven
senses.definitionCN: 人类生活与事务的世界，常与「天」相对
senses.example: He was the happiest man on earth that night.
senses.exampleCN: 那一夜他是世上最幸福的人。
senses.why: Once earth names the whole planet, it can also name the whole of human existence, the stage rather than the soil.
senses.whyCN: 当 earth 指整颗行星，它也能指整个人类存在的舞台，而不是土壤本身。

intro.en: Earth is one of the oldest native English nouns, and its ground sense predates its planetary sense.
intro.cn: earth 是英语最古老的本族名词之一，其「地面」义早于「行星」义。

items.en: A root often reconstructed as 'earth, ground' is widely accepted, but the details of its descent are uncertain.
items.cn: 通常重构的「土地、地面」词根被广泛接受，但其演变细节不确定。

items.en: A Germanic noun for the ground or soil is reconstructed and survives across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「土地、土壤」的日耳曼语名词，并在各日耳曼语言中留存。

items.en: Eorþe meant the ground, the soil, the land, and could already stand for the world.
items.cn: eorþe 意为地面、土壤、陆地，也可以已经指整个世界。

items.en: The spelling changed several times before settling as earth, with the same range of senses.
items.cn: 拼写几经变化才固定为 earth，义项范围基本未变。

items.en: Science made the planet sense dominant, while farming and travel kept the soil and land senses alive.
items.cn: 科学让「行星」义占据主导，农业与航海则让「土壤」与「陆地」义继续存活。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words beginning with the same letters; the near-meaning group gathers words for ground, soil and the planet.
note.cn: 形近组收开头字母相同的词；近义组收表示「地面」「土壤」与「行星」的词。

entries.definition: The organ of hearing, or the head of a grain plant.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉器官，或谷物的穗头。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning before the usual time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼副词，义为「早的、提早的」。

entries.definition: A sudden violent shaking of the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 地面的突然剧烈震动，即地震。

entries.definition: The upper layer of earth in which plants grow.
entries.definitionCN: 地表供植物生长的上层土壤。

entries.definition: The solid surface of the earth underfoot.
entries.definitionCN: 脚下坚实的地面。

entries.definition: The earth as a round whole, or a model of it.
entries.definitionCN: 作为圆球的整个地球，或其模型。

normalIntro.en: These hooks go from a handful of soil to the whole planet, then to land, the human world and the wiring sense.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一把土走到整颗行星，再到陆地、人间与接线的用法。

normal.en: Earth is first what is under the feet, then what is under the whole sky.
normal.cn: earth 先是脚下之物，后来成了整个天空之下之物。

normal.en: A handful of earth is the same substance microworlds are made of, seen from far away.
normal.cn: 手里一把土，与远看时的整个星球是同一物质。

normal.en: From a boat, earth is simply the part that is not water.
normal.cn: 从船上看，earth 就是那片不是水的部分。

normal.en: On earth can mean the whole human stage, not only the planet.
normal.cn: on earth 可以指整个人间舞台，而不只是这颗行星。

normal.en: To earth a wire is to send its charge into the ground, as a safe return.
normal.cn: 把电线 earth，就是把电荷送进大地，作为安全的回路。

abstract.en: Picture a fist of dark soil held up against a window showing a blue globe.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头握起黑土，举到一扇映着蓝色地球的窗前。

abstract.en: The same word can be soil, land, planet, world, or a safe electrical path.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以是土壤、陆地、行星、人世，或一条安全的电路。

abstract.en: Earth means the solid, the near, the place from which everything else is measured.
abstract.cn: earth 意味着坚实、靠近，以及衡量其他一切时所依据的那个位置。

examples.cn: 地球在空间站窗下缓缓转动。

examples.en: She pressed a handful of earth around the seedling.
examples.cn: 她把一把土按在幼苗周围。

examples.en: After weeks at sea, the sailors sighted earth.
examples.cn: 在海上漂了几周后，水手们看见了陆地。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of earth widen from a handful of soil to the planet, then to dry land and the whole human world.
sensesIntro.cn: earth 的四个义项从一把土扩大到整颗行星，再到干燥的陆地与整个人间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fist of dark soil is held up against a window showing a blue globe.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只拳头握起黑土，举到映着蓝色地球的窗前。

branches.en: THE PLANET: the whole globe, seen from space as one round body.
branches.cn: 行星线：整颗球体，从太空看是一个完整的圆。

branches.en: THE SOIL: the concrete substance that can be dug and carried.
branches.cn: 土壤线：能被挖起、搬走的具体物质。

branches.en: THE LAND: the dry surface that sailors look for after weeks at sea.
branches.cn: 陆线：水手在海上漂了数周后所寻找的干燥表面。

branches.en: THE WORLD: the whole stage of human life, often set against heaven.
branches.cn: 人间线：人类生活的整个舞台，常与「天」相对。

branches.en: THE SCALE: the same substance appears as a handful in the palm and as a planet in the window.
branches.cn: 尺度线：同一物质在掌心是一把土，在窗外是一颗行星。

intro.en: Earth is native Old English; English builds adjectives, a person-noun and compounds from it.
intro.cn: earth 是古英语本族词，英语由它构成形容词、指人名词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for the noun; the scientific vocabulary later borrowed separate Latin terms for the planet.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名词没有拉丁语来源；科学词汇后来另借拉丁术语指称这颗行星。

definition_zh: 地震；剧烈动荡
definition_en: a sudden violent shaking of the ground caused by movements within the earth, or a comparably violent upheaval
core_image: 碗柜忽然左右晃动，墙上的灰一层层落下
scene: 凌晨的屋子里，碗柜突然左右晃动。The earthquake lasted only forty seconds but cracked every wall.
sceneCN: 这里 earthquake 是「地震」（第 1 个义项：地壳运动引起的地面剧烈震动）；句意为地震只持续了四十秒，却裂开了每一面墙。图中可辨识物件：碗柜、裂缝、落灰。

pos.zh: 名词：地震；剧烈动荡

derivatives.zh: 由前缀与本词复合构成，义为「微震」
由本词与 proof 复合构成，义为「抗震的」

senses.title: A shaking of the ground
senses.definition: a sudden strong shaking of the ground caused by movement along faults in the earth's crust
senses.definitionCN: 地壳沿断层运动所引起的突然而强烈的地面震动
senses.example: The earthquake lasted only forty seconds but cracked every wall.
senses.exampleCN: 地震只持续了四十秒，却裂开了每一面墙。
senses.why: The word is a plain compound of earth and quake: the ground itself does the shaking that usually belongs to a hand or a voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 earth 与 quake 直接复合：本是手或声音才有的「抖动」，这里由地面自己来做。

senses.title: A violent upheaval
senses.titleCN: 剧烈动荡：比喻性的震动
senses.definition: a violent and far-reaching change in a society, market or system, compared to a physical quake
senses.definitionCN: 社会、市场或制度中猛烈而影响深远的变动，被比作真正的地震
senses.example: The new tax caused an earthquake in the housing market.
senses.exampleCN: 新税在房地产市场引发了一场地震。
senses.why: A real quake topples what looked solid, and the metaphor borrows exactly that: an upheaval that brings structures down.
senses.whyCN: 真正的地震会掀翻看似坚固的东西，比喻借的正是这一点：一场把结构掀倒的动荡。

intro.en: Earthquake is an English compound of two native words, and older English had other ways of naming the same event.
intro.cn: earthquake 是两个本族词构成的英语复合词，更早的英语还用别的方式称呼同一现象。

items.en: Eorþbeofung, literally 'earth-shaking', and eorþdyne, 'earth-din', named the event before the modern compound appeared.
items.cn: eorþbeofung（字面「地抖」）与 eorþdyne（「地响」）在现代复合词出现之前就已指称这一现象。

items.en: The compound earth plus quake is recorded in the fourteenth century, though the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: earth 加 quake 的复合形式见于十四世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word settled into its modern spelling and became the ordinary term in news and science.
items.cn: 这个词固定为现代拼写，并成为新闻与科学中的通用术语。

items.en: Seismology added precise vocabulary, but earthquake remained the everyday word and the base of metaphors.
items.cn: 地震学增加了精确术语，但 earthquake 仍是日常用词，也是比喻的基底。

items.en: Figurative use is common in business writing, where a policy can be said to cause an earthquake.
items.cn: 比喻用法在商业写作中很常见，一项政策就可以被说成引发地震。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on earth; the near-meaning group gathers words for quakes and upheavals.
note.cn: 形近组收以 earth 构成的复合词；近义组收表示震动与剧变的词。

entries.definition: The ground, the soil, or the planet itself.
entries.definitionCN: 地面、土壤，或行星本身。

entries.definition: A worm that lives in the soil.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在土壤里的蚯蚓。

entries.definition: A verb or noun for shaking, now mostly literary or technical.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「震动」的动词或名词，现多用于书面或技术语境。

entries.definition: A small or local shaking of the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微或局部的地面震动。

entries.definition: A violent change or disruption, often social or political.
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈的变动或扰乱，多指社会或政治方面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a cupboard rattling at night and end with a market shaken by a new rule.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从夜里作响的碗柜开始，到被新规震动的市场结束。

normal.en: Earthquake is the ground doing what a hand does: quaking.
normal.cn: earthquake 就是地面做出手才做的动作：抖动。

normal.en: Walls crack first because they are stiff, and stiff things break under a shake.
normal.cn: 墙先裂，因为它硬，而硬的东西在震动下会断。

normal.en: Aftershocks keep the fear going after the first forty seconds.
normal.cn: 第一次四十秒过后，余震还在延续恐惧。

normal.en: Call a tax change an earthquake and you are saying it toppled structures.
normal.cn: 把税制变动称作 earthquake，就是在说它掀翻了结构。

normal.en: Earthquake is a compound, so its meaning is visible: earth plus shake.
normal.cn: earthquake 是复合词，意思看得见：大地加上抖动。

abstract.en: Picture a level tabletop suddenly lifted at one corner while every object on it slides.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平桌的一角突然被抬起，桌上的东西全都滑落。

abstract.en: The same motion can be geological, or it can be a market, a party or a career.
abstract.cn: 同一种运动可以是地质的，也可以发生在市场、政党或职业生涯里。

abstract.en: Earthquake means the solid ground stops being a reliable base.
abstract.cn: earthquake 意味着坚实的地面不再是可靠的基底。

examples.en: The earthquake lasted only forty seconds but cracked every wall.
examples.cn: 地震只持续了四十秒，却裂开了每一面墙。

examples.en: The new tax caused an earthquake in the housing market.
examples.cn: 新税在房地产市场引发了一场地震。

examples.en: Thousands of earthquake survivors still live in temporary shelters.
examples.cn: 数千名地震幸存者仍住在临时安置点。

root: earthquake 由本族词 earth「大地」与 quake「抖动」复合而成，十四世纪见于文献；古英语另有 eorþbeofung 等说法。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses of earthquake: the literal shaking of the crust, and the borrowed image of any upheaval that topples solid structures.
sensesIntro.cn: earthquake 的两个义项：字面上地壳的震动，以及借来的意象——任何掀翻坚固结构的剧变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a level tabletop is jerked at one corner and everything on it slides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张平桌的一角被猛然抬起，桌上一切随之滑动。

branches.en: THE CRUST: the literal event, caused by movement along a fault.
branches.cn: 地壳线：字面事件，由断层运动引起。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a policy or shock that topples structures the way a quake topples walls.
branches.cn: 市场线：一项政策或冲击掀倒结构，正如地震掀倒墙。

branches.en: THE AFTERMATH: survivors, shelters and cracked walls belong to the literal event.
branches.cn: 灾后线：幸存者、安置点与裂墙都属于字面事件。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: the same word carries the fear of solid ground failing.
branches.cn: 比喻线：同一个词带着「坚固地面失灵」的恐惧。

branches.en: THE COLLAPSE: in both cases what looked stable suddenly gives way.
branches.cn: 崩塌线：两种情况下，看似稳定的东西都突然让位。

intro.en: Earthquake is a compound of two native words, so its affix work is mostly compounding plus a little prefixing.
intro.cn: earthquake 是两个本族词构成的复合词，所以其构词主要靠复合，外加少量前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the scientific terms around earthquakes, not the word itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供的是围绕地震的科学术语，而不是这个词本身。

items.example: The first element names what shakes.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分指明震动的是什么。

items.example: The second element names the action.
It forms aftershock, the word for later tremors.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 aftershock，指随后的余震。

scene: 老木匠闭着眼推刨子，木屑卷成均匀的卷。She eased the drawer open without a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 ease 是「缓缓地使（某物）松开、移动」（第 5 个义项：轻缓地移动或打开）；句意为她无声地把抽屉缓缓拉开。图中可辨识物件：刨子、木屑、抽屉。
